questions.prompt: A patient on modafinil is scheduled for an MSLT and the medication list was not reviewed until the morning of testing. What is the best technologist action?
options: Change the MSLT to CPAP titration independently
Proceed silently because modafinil has no effect on MSLT
Tell the patient to double the dose to stay awake
Notify/follow lab protocol and document the medication because wake-promoting agents can affect sleep latency
questions.answer: Notify/follow lab protocol and document the medication because wake-promoting agents can affect sleep latency
questions.rationale: Wake-promoting agents can alter sleep latency; medication information must be documented and handled by protocol.
questions.whyTricky: The trap is assuming a medication list is administrative rather than clinically important.
questions.coachBobNote: MSLT is fragile. Medications can bend the result.

questions.prompt: A patient reports taking an opioid and a sedative before the study. Which is the best technologist-level response?
options: Document the substances, monitor carefully, and follow safety/protocol escalation if respiratory depression or concerning events occur
Score all respiratory events as obstructive without reviewing effort
Ignore them because the physician ordered the PSG
Tell the patient to take more medication if they cannot sleep
questions.answer: Document the substances, monitor carefully, and follow safety/protocol escalation if respiratory depression or concerning events occur
questions.rationale: Sedating medications and opioids can affect respiration/arousability and must be documented and monitored within protocol.
questions.whyTricky: The trap is treating medications as irrelevant once the study starts.
questions.coachBobNote: Medication history is part of the tracing.

questions.prompt: A night-shift worker reports insomnia when trying to sleep during the day and sleepiness during work hours. What is the best assessment habit?
options: Assume OSA is the only possible cause
Tell the patient to quit the job
Document work schedule, sleep timing, light exposure, and symptoms as possible circadian/shift-work context
Ignore schedule because PSG channels will answer everything
questions.answer: Document work schedule, sleep timing, light exposure, and symptoms as possible circadian/shift-work context
questions.rationale: Sleep schedule and circadian context are key parts of patient assessment, especially for shift workers.
questions.whyTricky: The trap is forcing every sleep complaint into an OSA-only frame.
questions.coachBobNote: Sleep has a clock. Ask about the clock.

questions.prompt: A patient reports drinking alcohol before the study. Why does that matter for the record?
options: Alcohol can alter sleep architecture, respiratory events, arousal threshold, and interpretation context
Alcohol improves PSG validity because it helps sleep onset
Alcohol means the study must always be canceled

questions.rationale: Alcohol can affect sleep and breathing and should be documented for interpretation context.
questions.whyTricky: The trap is treating pre-study alcohol as either helpful or automatically disqualifying without protocol.
questions.coachBobNote: Document the clue; do not pretend the night happened in a vacuum.

questions.prompt: A patient with morbid obesity, morning headaches, and chronic daytime hypercapnia is ordered for PSG with CO2 monitoring. What should the technologist anticipate?
options: That oximetry alone fully evaluates ventilation
That PAP is contraindicated in all obese patients
Possible sleep-related hypoventilation/OHS context requiring careful ventilation monitoring per order
A routine insomnia-only study with no respiratory concern
questions.answer: Possible sleep-related hypoventilation/OHS context requiring careful ventilation monitoring per order
questions.rationale: History can indicate hypoventilation risk; CO2 monitoring helps assess ventilation rather than oxygenation alone.
questions.whyTricky: The trap is relying on SpO2 alone or ignoring daytime hypercapnia.
questions.coachBobNote: Morning headaches and CO2 are not throwaway details.
